summary: Laos admits fellow ASEAN nationals visa-free for up to 30 days (14 for Myanmar), plus Japan, South Korea, Russia, Switzerland and others on bilateral or unilateral waivers. Nearly everyone else gets a 30-day tourist visa easily — online through the official Lao eVisa or on arrival at major airports and border crossings. About 35 nationalities that are not on the eVisa list, mostly in Africa and the Middle East plus Pakistan, Bangladesh and Iran, should apply at a Lao embassy.

tips.text: Bring crisp US dollar notes. They are accepted for many tourist services and are a useful backup where ATMs are unreliable.

The Lao eVisa is accepted only at designated entry points — Vientiane and Luang Prabang airports and a handful of land crossings such as the first Friendship Bridge. Check the official list before planning an overland entry.
Unexploded ordnance from the 1960s-70s still contaminates parts of eastern and southern Laos. Stay on marked paths and roads in rural areas and never touch metal objects found on the ground.
The kip has depreciated sharply in recent years, so prices for tours and hotels are often quoted in US dollars or Thai baht. Carry a mix and check which currency a quote is in.
Cover shoulders and knees at temples, remove shoes before entering, and be discreet during the dawn alms round in Luang Prabang. Keep your distance and never disrupt the monks.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Laos?
faq.answer: ASEAN nationals enter visa-free (30 days for most members, 14 for Myanmar), and Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Russia and Mongolia have bilateral or unilateral waivers. Almost everyone else — including US, UK, EU, Canadian and Australian passport holders — gets a 30-day tourist visa either online via laoevisa.gov.la or on arrival at major entry points. Nationalities missing from the eVisa list should apply at a Lao embassy.

faq.question: Should I get the Lao eVisa or a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Both give a 30-day single-entry tourist stay. The eVisa (USD 50, about three business days online) skips the arrival line but is accepted only at designated checkpoints; the visa on arrival is issued at major entry points, such as international airports and border crossings. No official page publishes its fee.

faq.question: Can I use the Lao eVisa at any border crossing?
faq.answer: No. It is honored only at designated entry points, including Vientiane's Wattay and Luang Prabang international airports and the first Lao-Thai Friendship Bridge. Arriving anywhere else, get a visa on arrival or an embassy visa instead; check the current list on laoevisa.gov.la.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Laos?
faq.answer: Yes. Tourist visas can be extended at most twice per arrival at the Department of Immigration in Vientiane or a provincial immigration office (the Department's visa page says a visa on arrival can be extended once); no maximum length per extension is published. Apply at least 3 days before your stay expires; the fee is 20,000 kip per day plus 40,000 kip per application, and it takes 1-2 business days. Visa-exempt stays cannot be extended except in emergencies, with supporting documents. Overstays are fined per day on departure.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Laos?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders are not visa-exempt. Apply online for the Lao eVisa (USD 50) before travel or obtain a 30-day tourist visa on arrival at major airports and border crossings.
